South Carolina Republican Presidential Primary Filing Fee is $40,000

Candidates file with the party, but, by law, the party gives $20,000 of that fee to the government to help pay for election administration. The party keeps the other $20,000 and the party need not pay any election administration costs for its primary.

Okay, seems reasonable without looking at the cost in other states. Half to the state for administration and half to their party so the party can handle the smaller details of the primary. $20k is chump change to the government, but that's $20k less that tax payers have to shell out to cover the cost of someone running for President.
Good points. To me, the story more speaks to how these filing fees limit fuller participation. So, I kind of interpret from a 'third party' perspective.

Yeah, I thought about that too. I of course acknowledge that no one running for public office should be denied based upon money.... but it costs a hell of a lot of money to run for office, much less, the Presidency. Of course some of that cost comes from this exact fee, but it's hardly comparable to the cost of putting out advertisements. So someone who isn't able to afford these fees will probably not have much of a chance anyways.
